speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've been having episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing; to understand what's happening, how long does each episode last and do you lose consciousness?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from generalized absence seizures). The history of brief staring spells with impaired awareness, post-ictal lethargy, and a specific prodrome (muddy taste) is highly suggestive of focal seizures with secondary generalization or complex partial seizures, rather than typical absence status which usually presents as continuous staring without post-ictal confusion. I need to confirm the semiology and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST IMAGES: None at this time.

How old is the boy, and have there been any fevers, head injuries, or known seizures in his family history? Also, do these episodes occur only when he is awake and alert, or can they happen while he is sleeping?
